lines.text: Welcome to Delegate Demystified.
Today's topic is UiPath Delegate, described as your first AI intern.
It is a digital sidekick that learns from you, and does real work across your apps.
By the end, you will know what it does, how you teach it, and how you stay in control.
Meet Sam. Sam has a problem.
A pile of busywork: email digests, [CRM|C R M] updates, smart reporting, and asset creation.
AI can remove that busywork, but only if it knows how to work inside a real company.
That is the problem Delegate is designed to tackle.
So, Sam hires an intern.
So, what is Delegate?
It goes beyond suggestions. It gets tasks completed, from start to finish.
First, it offloads the busywork: repetitive admin work that drains your time and focus.
Second, work gets done, not just suggested.
Third, it is a trainable sidekick, with skills that grow with how you work.
Fourth, it is enterprise ready: reliable, secure, and aware of your workflows.
How do you hand work to Delegate? There are four ways.
You can type a prompt.
You can speak a command.
You can record your screen.
Or you can start from a template.
Behind the scenes, it is a general purpose agent with computer use, working across browsers and apps.
It runs programmatically, with enterprise grade reliability.
Where does it pay off? Here are three top enterprise use cases.
One: PDD and SDD generation.
Define processes, contact [SMEs|subject matter experts], record their tasks, and sign off on documents.
Then hand them to Autopilot and coding agents, to build the solution.
Two: application testing.
Run test cases, set up environments, run exploratory testing, and refine object repositories.
Three: personal productivity.
Triage incoming work, and validate and follow up on missing evidence.
Then resolve escalations and duplicates.
Two more are listed as future: internal enablement, and discovery.
Enablement would run training on demand, plugged into your knowledge, docs, and goals.
Discovery would surface tribal know-how across teams. The more you use it, the better it gets.
Why would a company choose Delegate to increase employee productivity?
Here are the four reasons UiPath gives.
One: best in class UI automation.
It is built on the same UiPath UIA foundation as RPA.
UiPath says that makes it more reliable on enterprise apps than tools that only look at the screen.
And it adds skills, steering, and multi app orchestration on top.
Two: it is built as an extension, on top of your existing UiPath deployment.
UiPath says that means no new IT approval, and no new upgrade process.
The UiPath Assistant simply upgrades into Delegate.
Three: structural governance.
Every operation runs through the same access control, audit trail, credential vault, and AI Trust Layer.
Governance is built in, not bolted on.
Four: more automation, and more capacity.
Discover and document processes, do more testing, and free people for higher value automation work.
Let's follow a day with Delegate, for a Product Support Engineer, or [PSE|P S E].
Eight prompts take the engineer from backlog to resolution.
Morning planning. Pull my case backlog from Salesforce, and prioritize the day.
Delegate pulls the cases, and puts the day in order.
Context awareness. Summarize the case I'm viewing, with related articles and similar past cases.
One summary, with everything related attached.
License lookup. Look up a customer's licensing data, without switching tools.
The answer arrives in the chat. No tab hopping.
Log analysis. Pull recent App Insights logs for a tenant, without navigating Azure.
The logs come to you. No digging through Azure.
Troubleshooting research. Search product docs, the knowledge base, Slack, Confluence, and past cases at once.
One question. Five places searched at the same time.
First response drafting. Generate a reply from the case context, to edit and send to Salesforce.
A draft reply, ready to polish and send.
[RunDeck|Run Deck] jobs. Run a predefined job with parameters, without leaving the workflow.
Set the parameters, and the job runs, right inside the workflow.
And stay in flow.
One conversational surface, across every tool the [PSE|P S E] touches.
Now let's look at how it works, from prompt to productivity.
There are four things Delegate does for you.
First, it composes and executes tasks.
You write instructions in plain language. No code.
It breaks a complex workflow into steps.
It handles UI automation, files, and API calls.
And it learns from your feedback over time.
Second, you teach it skills, with Routines.
A routine captures your expertise as a reusable playbook.
Document a workflow once, and invoke it forever.
Share skills across the team, for consistency.
Your custom skills are always on tap.
Third, you can attach your [SOPs|S O Ps], and invoke automations.
Reference your [SOPs|S O Ps] directly.
Link your design documents, for context.
Invoke deployed UiPath automations.
And view the complete task trail and history.
Fourth, you control what Delegate can access.
Use allow and deny lists for apps and [URLs|U R Ls].
Set granular permissions by task type.
Every action Delegate takes is recorded in an audit trail.
And your data stays in your control.
You also decide how much freedom Delegate has, per environment and per task.
There are three modes.
Mode one is Always ask. This is the safest.
Delegate confirms every action before it runs, so you have full oversight on every step.
Mode two is Smart. This is the balanced mode.
Delegate decides based on the risk level of each action, and asks only when it matters.
Mode three is Unrestricted. This gives full autonomy.
Use it with caution. Only in trusted environments.
Quick check. Which mode confirms every action before it runs?
Always ask.
Underneath it all, Delegate is governed by design.
Every operation inherits the controls you already run UiPath with.
Orchestrator handles central scheduling, queues, and run management for every agent operation.
The credential vault keeps secrets encrypted and brokered, and never exposed to the agent.
The AI Trust Layer applies policy, redaction, and model governance to every interaction.
And role based access covers all operations, mapped to your existing organization.
The same controls apply to every action, automatically.
Let's recap.
You hand Delegate work by prompt, by voice, by screen recording, or from a template.
Teach Delegate once with Routines, and share those skills across your team.
And you stay in control, with three modes, and governance built in.
Delegate the busywork. Keep the judgment.
Thanks for watching.
